title: Mets to start Tobias Myers instead of David Peterson vs. Cubs
content:
On a 10-game losing streak, the New York Mets are making their first major change to the back end of their rotation.

In place of struggling lefty David Peterson, an All-Star last season, right-hander Tobias Myers is set to start Sunday’s game against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field, the club announced.

Peterson is available in the bullpen, people familiar with the Mets’ plans said.

Peterson, the Mets’ longest-tenured player, is coming off three poor starts. After Peterson’s last start, however, Mets manager Carlos Mendoza noted that his stuff looked better. Still, the results were not good. Against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday, Peterson allowed four runs, five hits and four walks in five innings. His ERA stands at 6.41.

After his All-Star appearance last season, things fell apart for Peterson. In 12 starts during the second half, he posted a 6.34 ERA. Peterson, 30, is set to be a free agent after the season.

The hope is for Myers to make it through the batting order one time. He last pitched Wednesday, throwing two innings and 30 pitches. Myers holds plenty of experience as a starting pitcher, but he is not fully stretched out. He hasn’t pitched more than three innings in a game this season.

The secondary piece in the Mets’ trade with the Milwaukee Brewers for Freddy Peralta, Myers has pitched well as a long man out of the bullpen this year. His 3.46 ERA doesn’t tell the whole story, as he has permitted just 10 base runners in 13 innings and at one point retired 31 of 33 hitters.

“What makes him really unique and special is his high velo and high slot, so everything looks the same out of hand,” pitching coach Justin Willard said last week. “We’re just getting to some slightly different shapes than he had previously: a little more cut on the cutter, a little more drop on the splitter, and then morphing the previous slider and curveball into the same pitch where it’s harder and has more depth.

“It’s really platoon-neutral. Whether it’s a one-inning stint or for five or six innings, it should be able to play.”

Myers owns a career 3.17 ERA in 31 starts in the majors. He was a regular starter for Milwaukee in 2024, when he posted a 3.00 ERA over 138 innings and held the Mets scoreless through five innings in a winner-take-all playoff game that October.

The Mets have not yet made a decision on Kodai Senga, who has fared worse than Peterson lately. Over Senga’s last two starts, he has allowed 14 runs in just 5 2/3 innings.

The last time the Mets (7-14) lost 10 or more games in a row was an 11-game slide in 2004.
